THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 04.12.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:
This is an application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
2. The petitioner is accused No.15 in Crime No. RC 4 & 5(S)/2013/CBI/SCB, Thiruvananthapuram.

The offences alleged against the petitioner and the other accused are punishable under Sections 120(B) r/w Section 342, 343, 365, 366, 368, 376 & 420 of IPC and Sections 3(1), 4(1), 5(1) and 6(1)
of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956.
3.

The prosecution case, as narrated in Annexure 2 order, reads thus:-
"In the year 2010, accused No.15/petitioner, who was an inmate of the brothel conducted by accused No.2, entered into a conspiracy with accused Nos. I to 3 to recruit girls to the brothel run by them in the UAE.

In prosecution of that conspiracy,
accused No. 15/petitioner induced the victim by offering her a job as a housemaid in Dubai with a salary of 25,000/- to 30,000/-, and then sent the victim to Dubai,
knowing that on reaching Dubai, she would be taken to the brothel run by accused Nos. 1 to 3.
On reaching the UAE, the victim was taken to the brothel of accused No. 2 and was used for prostitution forcefully.

"

sentences.text: The petitioner was arrested on 10.10.2025 and she has been in judicial custody since then.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Special Public Prosecutor appearing for the CBI.
6.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the long exile of the petitioner in the Middle East was due to reasons beyond her control.
The learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner is prepared to co-operate with the trial.
7. The learned Special Public Prosecutor opposed the bail plea of the petitioner on the ground that there is no possibility that the petitioner will co-operate with the trial.
8. The learned Special Public Prosecutor brought to my notice that the petitioner had remained absconding for a long period of 13  years.
9. The petitioner is a lady aged 52 years.
The prosecution case as narrated in the impugned order reveals that the petitioner was an inmate of the brothel conducted by accused No.2.
The further allegation is that she also 2025:KER:93798 became part of a conspiracy to recruit girls to the Middle East for the purpose of prostitution.
10. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner never had the mens rea in the commission of the offences.
She only happened to be under the clutches of the other accused.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that due to the dire need to earn her livelihood, she remained in the Middle East working as a housemaid.
11. The petitioner made an undertaking that she will regularly appear before the Court and face trial.
She further made an undertaking that she will appear before the SHO, Mandrothuruthu Police Station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m. till the trial is over.
12. I have taken note of the entire materials including the circumstances in which this lady involved in the offences alleged.
This Court is of the considered view that a custodial trial is not required.

In view of the specific undertaking made on the part of the petitioner that she will 2025:KER:93798 co-operate with the trial, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled to be released on bail on conditions.

In the result, the Bail Application is allowed as follows:
(a) The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail on her executing bond for Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional court.

sentences.text: (b) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on every Sunday between 10 A.M. and 11 A.M. till the trial is over.
(c) The petitioner shall surrender her passport before the jurisdictional court.
(d) The petitioner shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the jurisdictional court.
(e) The petitioner shall not commit any similar offence while on bail.
(f) The petitioner shall not try to influence the prosecution witnesses or attempt to tamper with the evidence.
(g) If any of the bail conditions are violated by the petitioner, the jurisdictional Court will be at liberty to cancel the bail, in accordance with law.
